title: Colour theory: hue, saturation and lightness

videos.script: Every colour on a screen is three numbers: how much red, how much green, how much blue. That is how the screen makes it. It is not how anyone thinks about it. {{rgb}} People describe colour in three different questions. Which colour is it: red, green, blue? That is hue. How strong is it, against grey? That is saturation. How light or dark is it? That is lightness. {{three}} Charts use all three, and lightness matters most. It is the one the eye reads as more or less. {{lightness}} Here is a trap. Take pure yellow and pure blue. The usual colour picker calls both of them fifty per cent lightness. Now turn them to grey. Yellow is almost white. Blue is almost black. {{trap}} The picker is not measuring what the eye sees. Newer colour spaces do, and they are what good palettes are built in. {{spaces}} This lesson explains the three dimensions, shows where the familiar ones lie, and gives you a way to measure a colour yourself. {{plan}}
